title: Foundations of Home and Host Supervision
summary: Why cross-border groups need cooperating supervisors, how responsibilities are allocated between home and host, and the risks of supervisory gaps and duplication.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why cross-border groups need cooperating supervisors, how responsibilities are allocated between home and host, and the risks of supervisory gaps and duplication.
Learning Objectives: Explain the home-host principle in the Basel Core Principles and other sector standards
Distinguish home and host supervisor roles and responsibilities
Identify the risks of gaps, duplication and conflicting demands
Syllabus: Basel Core Principles, IAIS and IOSCO standards on cross-border cooperation
Allocation of home and host responsibilities across sectors
Asymmetry: large home, small host and systemic branches
Supervisory gaps, regulatory arbitrage and duplication
Intended Audience: Supervisors responsible for cross-border groups, branches, subsidiaries or third-country firms
International affairs, legal and cooperation staff managing MoUs and information requests
Senior supervisors and managers who represent the authority in colleges and crisis management groups
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of prudential or conduct supervision is helpful. No prior involvement in colleges or international cooperation is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Supervisory Colleges (2014)
IOSCO, Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU) and Enhanced MMoU (2016)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
IAIS, Insurance Core Principles and Common Framework for the Supervision of Internationally Active Insurance Groups (ComFrame)
